sections.label: Land as scarce resource
sections.summary: Land in Singapore is described as a scarce and finite national resource.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Land in Singapore is a scarce and finite national resource.

sections.label: Bill on urban renewal
sections.summary: The Bill builds on previous efforts to keep the urban renewal framework fit for purpose and allow orderly, sustainable renewal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: That is not a good outcome for residents and it is also not a good outcome for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This Bill builds upon previous efforts to ensure that our framework for urban renewal remains fit for purpose – to cater for ageing developments a viable pathway forward where there is support amongst owners for redevelopment and allow for Singapore's urban landscape to continue to renew itself in an orderly and sustainable fashion.

sections.label: Single holdout blocking sale
sections.summary: A single holdout could thwart the wishes of all other owners and prevent the sale from proceeding entirely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A single holdout – for whatever reason, whether principled or otherwise – could thwart the wishes of all the other owners and prevent the sale from proceeding with entirely.

sections.label: 1999 collective sale consent thresholds
sections.summary: In 1999 Parliament amended the Land Titles (Strata) Act to allow collective sales with 80% consent for developments aged 10 years or more and 90% for those under 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 1999, Parliament amended the Land Titles (Strata) Act to allow collective sales if: 80% consent was obtained for developments aged 10 years or more, and 90% for those less than 10 years old.

sections.label: Older non-landed private units
sections.summary: About one in 20 non-landed private residential units are now aged 40 years or older, around 20,000 dwelling units in close to 250 developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Approximately one in 20 non-landed private residential units are now aged 40 years or older, and that is around 20,000 dwelling units in close to 250 developments.

sections.label: Cost of modernising a lift
sections.summary: The estimated cost of modernising a single lift starts from $120,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The estimated cost of modernising a single lift starts from $120,000.

sections.label: Raising maintenance fees and sinking fund
sections.summary: Maintenance fees and sinking fund contributions may need to be raised significantly as developments age, in some cases by as much as 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To fund this, it is only logical for maintenance fees and sinking fund contributions to be raised significantly as developments age – in some cases by as much as 50%.

sections.label: Hong Kong compulsory sale regime
sections.summary: Hong Kong's compulsory sale regime for redevelopment, the Land (Compulsory Sale for Redevelopment) Ordinance, came into effect in 1999 like Singapore's collective sale regime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Their equivalent of the collective sale regime is the compulsory sale regime for redevelopment – the Land (Compulsory Sale for Redevelopment) Ordinance – that, like Singapore's collective sale regime, came into effect in 1999.

sections.label: New consent thresholds by development age
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a 70% threshold for developments aged 40 to 59 years and 65% for those 60 years and older, while existing 90% and 80% thresholds continue for newer developments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces two new tiers: for developments aged 40 to 59 years, a new threshold of 70%; for developments aged 60 years and older, a new threshold of 65%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The existing 90% and 80% consent thresholds that you see today in the legislation will continue to apply to newer developments, those below 10 years old and those from 10 to 39 years old, respectively.

sections.label: Higher requisition threshold and shorter CSA period
sections.summary: The Bill raises the requisition threshold for forming a Collective Sale Committee to 35% of owners and reduces the time to obtain Collective Sale Agreement signatures from 12 months to six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Currently, a requisition to convene an Extraordinary General Meeting for the formation of a Collective Sale Committee (CSC) must be signed by 20% of owners by share value, or 25% of owners by number of units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill raises this to 35% of owners by share value or number of units.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, we are reducing the time period that CSCs have to obtain signatures to the Collective Sale Agreement (CSA), from 12 months to six months.

sections.label: Longer restriction period after failed sale
sections.summary: The restriction period after a failed collective sale attempt is extended from two years to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, we are extending the restriction period after a failed collective sale attempt from two years to three years.

sections.label: Requisition threshold for subsequent attempts
sections.summary: For second or subsequent attempts, the requisition threshold will align with the applicable overall consent threshold based on development age, 70% for ages 40 to 59 and 65% for 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For any second or subsequent attempt, the requisition threshold will be aligned to the applicable overall consent threshold based on the age of the development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, in this case, 70% for developments aged 40 to 59 years old, and 65% for developments aged 60 years and above.

sections.label: Collective sales for non-strata developments
sections.summary: New section 84FC allows collective sales for private wholly residential non-strata-titled developments when consent thresholds based on age are met, where flat owners hold leasehold under 850 years but do not own underlying land.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Specifically, the new section 84FC will allow collective sales when the consent thresholds based on the age of the development are met for private wholly residential non-strata-titled developments, where flat owners hold a leasehold tenure of less than 850 years in their units, but do not own the underlying land.

sections.label: Five MOF-owned developments divestment
sections.summary: Five developments with land owned by MOF (Inc) are named, and MOF (Inc) is prepared to divest its interest at fair market value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Specifically, five developments where the land is owned by the Minister for Finance, as incorporated under the Minister for Finance (Incorporation) Act 1959 (or MOF (Inc)).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These were developments that were sold as public sector staff benefits many decades ago or owned by Government for security reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These five are: Neptune Court, Townhouse Apartments, Orchard Court, One Tree Hill Mansions and Paterson Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MOF (Inc) is prepared to divest its interest in these developments at fair market value.

sections.label: Seven-month consent threshold deadline
sections.summary: They will have seven months from the commencement date to achieve the requisite consent threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In which case they will have seven months from the commencement date to achieve the requisite consent threshold.

sections.label: Smaller majority for older developments
sections.summary: A smaller majority of owners can now push through a collective sale if their strata-titled developments are 40 years or older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The practical effect is this: a smaller majority of owners will now be able to push through a collective sale if their strata-titled developments are 40 years or older.

sections.label: Three issues on the Bill
sections.summary: Three issues are raised: equitable safeguards for non-consenting owners, expediting Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act changes for sinking funds, and sufficiency for strata-titled developments with ultimate developer landowner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In this context, I wish to raise three issues in relation to the Bill: first, to consider further equitable safeguards for the larger minority of non-consenting owners; second, expediting upstream changes to the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act to mitigate the issue of inadequate sinking funds for maintenance and repair; third, whether these amendments are sufficient for strata-titled developments where subsidiary proprietors own a lease of 99 years or more but there is an ultimate developer landowner who owns the freehold tenure.

sections.label: Seller's stamp duty exemption request
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider exempting this class of home owners from seller's stamp duty, particularly if they purchased before the announcement of the lowered consent threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider exempting this class of home owners from seller's stamp duty, particularly if they had purchased their homes before the announcement of the lowering of the consent threshold?

sections.label: Strata maintenance fees and leasehold reversion
sections.summary: The passage asks about Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act changes and notes leasehold strata units with no lease top-up valuation mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The question for such home owners is no longer sell or stay, but sell or pay costly fees for maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This could be mitigated, however, by corresponding upstream changes to the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act to require MCSTs to build up and maintain their sinking funds for upgrading and maintenance works and/or ringfence monies for costly works, such as lift replacements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Town Councils for example are required to ring-fence a percentage of all Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) collections into a lift replacement fund and a minimum percentage of the same into an ordinary sinking fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In fact, earlier this year, the Government had announced a review of the Building Maintenance and Strata Management Act to address these issues, I would like to ask if the Minister could share if more details will be forthcoming soon and ideally, in tandem with the changes proposed here for the collective sale regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, I would like to highlight that class of strata-titled developments where the landowner developer of freehold land, develops and sells leasehold strata-titled units to home owners while retaining the reversion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: These do not represent a large stock of our private strata-titled developments, but significantly, unlike leasehold developments on Government land put out to tender for development, there is no valuation mechanism for a topping up of the lease, which is a crucial element in the viability of collective sale exercises.

sections.label: Lease top-up and consent thresholds
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a valuation-based mechanism could require the landowner to re-acquire or top up the lease, and notes consent thresholds adjusted by age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For such developments, I would like to ask the Minister if there are plans to address the situation, such as by setting a valuation-based mechanism, which mandates that the landowner either re-acquires the development by collective sale or agrees to top-up the lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By adjusting the consent thresholds required for collective sales based on the age of development, we are providing owners of older properties with a far more realistic and practical avenue to consider redevelopment.

sections.label: Ageing private residential developments
sections.summary: The passage states about one in 20 private non-landed units are over 40 years old and over 1,000 of 3,750 private developments are at least 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, about one in 20 private non-landed residential units are over 40 years of age, while more than 1,000 of Singapore's 3,750 private residential developments are at least 30 years old.

sections.label: Aljunied HUDC redevelopment examples
sections.summary: The passage states Affinity at Serangoon and The Minton were redeveloped with more than 1,000 units each on former HUDC estates of 244 and 342 units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC) for example, Affinity at Serangoon and The Minton were both redeveloped with more than 1,000 units, each on former HUDC estates that had 244 units and 342 units respectively.

sections.label: Safeguards for dissenting home owners
sections.summary: The passage welcomes safeguards in the Bill, including a shorter signature collection timeframe and an extended restriction period against repeated en bloc attempts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For many long-term residents, even with a successful en bloc payout, it may be virtually impossible to purchase a unit of comparable size, character and location in today's property market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thus, I welcome the safeguards built into this Bill to protect dissenting or hesitant home owners, such as a shorter timeframe that CSCs have to collect signatures for a CSA and an extended restriction period to prohibit repeated aggressive en bloc attempts where underlying support remains insufficient.

sections.label: Signature periods and upzoning proposals
sections.summary: The passage suggests longer signature collection periods for larger estates, a three-month extension, and active upzoning to encourage redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the signature collection period could be maintained at six months for smaller developments, but MinLaw could allow nine months for estates with more than 300 or 500 units to collect the requisite number of signatures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, if a CSC manages to reach within five percentage points of the requisite consent threshold at the end of the initial six months, they could automatically receive a one-off three-month extension to secure the remaining signatures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider these adjustments to ensure that larger estates are not unfairly penalised in obtaining the requisite number of signatures?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It gives older developments a viable mechanism to redevelopment and relieve asset-rich, cash-poor owners from crushing maintenance costs, while protecting home owners from unrelenting pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, to further enhance the effectiveness of this Bill, it should be coupled with active upzoning to create additional incentives for home owners and property developers to redevelop ageing developments and increase the availability of housing in mature estates throughout Singapore.

sections.label: Collective sale threshold and safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill lowers consent thresholds to 70% or 65% by age and adds safeguards including a shorter signature period and higher objector proceeds limit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore lowers the collective sale consent threshold to 70% or 65%, depending on the development's age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the same time, it offers counter-balancing safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It raises the level of support required to initiate the process, lengthens the cooling-off period following an unsuccessful attempt, shortens the signature period from 12 months to six months, and increases the percentage limit relevant to the Court's power to increase the proceeds payable to objectors.

sections.label: Vulnerable owner protection protocol
sections.summary: A collective sale premium may not cover moving difficulties or lost support networks, so the speaker asks for a vulnerable owner protection protocol.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A collective sale premium may compensate for the market value of the property, but it does not automatically compensate for the difficulty of moving, the loss of familiar support networks or the challenge of finding accessible replacement home easily.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I ask whether the Government will introduce a vulnerable owner protection protocol for the elderly, for those who are disabled and immobile owner occupiers.

sections.label: Plain language apportionment explanation
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will require a standard plain language explanation of the apportionment method.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider requiring a standard simple plain language explanation of apportionment method, including how strata area, share value and valuation affect different categories of units?

sections.label: Review of collective sale outcomes
sections.summary: The review should examine collective sale attempts, owner disputes, shorter signature period outcomes and replacement housing, balancing renewal with elderly residents' homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The review should examine the number and success rate of collective sale attempts, disputes between owners, the use of shorter signature period outcomes for dissenting and vulnerable residents, and whether owners were able to secure suitable replacement housing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A legitimate and durable collective sales system requires both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We should facilitate the renewal of ageing developments where broad support exists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But we should also remember that for an elderly resident, a home is not merely a parcel of redevelopment value.

sections.label: MinLaw expectations for lower thresholds
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to explain what MinLaw expects the lower thresholds of 70% and 65% to deliver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, I would like to ask the Government to explain what MinLaw expects these lower thresholds to deliver.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill lowers the consent thresholds to 70% for developments from 40 to under 60 years old; and to 65% from 60 years old onwards.

sections.label: Financial-loss test and safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government assessed owners who clear financial-loss and mortgage tests yet still face replacement difficulties, noting the pool rises to 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Objectors also have protections against statutory financial loss or being unable to redeem a mortgage or charge on their property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, because the financial-loss test is principally tied to the original purchase price of the property, an owner may clear the test and the mortgage, and yet, still have too little left for suitable replacement property somewhere else.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For a household that opposes a collective sale, it may still have to bear these costs despite wishing to remain in their home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I therefore ask whether the Government has assessed how many affected owners could clear the existing financial-loss and mortgage tests, yet still face difficulties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What safeguards does it consider adequate for them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill also expands the aggregate pool available for certain adjustments to sale proceeds, from 0.25% to 0.5%, while retaining the $2,000 floor as an alternative.

sections.label: VERS Bill and relocation options
sections.summary: The Minister agreed voting needed careful consideration and said relocation options were being studied, while the Bill puts a decision on lowering the renewal barrier and safeguards to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for National Development then agreed that voting required careful consideration because the stakes were higher than in an upgrading exercise and said that relocation options were also being studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today puts a closely related decision in Parliament's hands, about how far to lower the barrier to renewal and what safeguards should accompany the greater power of a majority to require others to leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: VERS will involve public funding, housing subsidy and state land.

sections.label: Households facing debt or savings
sections.summary: A majority may favour renewal while some households required to move face substantial new debt or a draw on retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A majority may favour renewal while some of the households required to move face substantial new debt or a draw on retirement savings.

sections.label: Proposed new voting thresholds
sections.summary: The Bill retains 90% and 80% thresholds for titles under 10 and 40 years, adding 70% for 40 to 60 years and 65% for over 60 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The proposed new thresholds in the Bill retain the existing threshold of 90% and 80% for titles less than 10 and 40 years old, but we now add a new, lower 70% threshold for leases between 40 and 60 years old, and another 65% level for developments over 60 years old.

sections.label: Landed housing lease percentages
sections.summary: A 2025 Parliamentary Question indicated about 14% of landed housing stock sits on 999-year leases and 73% on freehold leases.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A Parliamentary Question, filed in 2025, indicated that approximately 14% of landed housing stock sit on 999-year leases; and 73% on freehold leases.

sections.label: Support for non-consenting minority owners
sections.summary: The speaker asks what bridging support or relocation assistance can be extended to elderly or vulnerable minority owners compelled to give up their home, and whether a mediation mechanism will be established.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The recent removal of the 15-month wait-out period to purchase HDB flats will certainly help these owners to find a new home.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But can the Minister clarify: what specific bridging support or relocation assistance, if any, can be extended to elderly or vulnerable minority owners who did not consent to the sale, but are nonetheless compelled to give up their primary home under these lowered thresholds?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, will the Government establish a dedicated, independent mediation mechanism, together with a proper framework of financial and psychological support, to accompany this legislation?

sections.label: HIP and NRP thresholds
sections.summary: The Home Improvement Programme requires 75% in each block, while the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme takes a cluster view of the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Home Improvement Programme (HIP) requires 75% in each block, while the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) takes a cluster view of the threshold.

sections.label: 70% threshold for older flats
sections.summary: A 70% threshold for flats between 40 and 60 years old may already be a high bar to clear.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 70% threshold for flats between 40 and 60 years old may already be a high bar to clear.

sections.label: HDB owners reluctant to sell
sections.summary: HDB flat owners may be even more reluctant to sell, as seen in the Ang Mo Kio Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme episode.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This may mean that HDB flat owners may be even more reluctant to sell.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We saw this during the Ang Mo Kio's Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme episode where some owners were concerned to hear that they had to pay cash in order to buy a replacement flat of the same size nearby even though the economics may eventually have ultimately worked in their favour.

sections.label: Precedent for ageing public housing
sections.summary: Decisions made today may be a precedent for handling ageing public housing stock that houses a super-majority of citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The decisions we make today may also be a precedent for how we handle ageing public housing stock which makes up a super-majority of how we house our citizens.

sections.label: Consent thresholds by development age
sections.summary: For developments between 40 and 59 years old the consent threshold falls to 70%, and for those 60 years and above it falls to 65%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For developments between 40 and 59 years old, the consent threshold falls to 70%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For those aged 60 years and above, it falls further to 65%.

sections.label: VERS for selected HDB precincts
sections.summary: VERS, based on what has been announced so far, is intended for selected HDB precincts around the age of 70.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: VERS, based on what has been announced so far, is intended for selected HDB precincts around the age of 70.

sections.label: Wait-out period removed
sections.summary: The 15-month wait-out period for eligible private home owners buying non-subsidised HDB resale flats has recently been removed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The 15-month wait-out period for eligible private home owners buying non-subsidised HDB resale flats has recently been removed.

sections.label: Housing support for larger families
sections.summary: The Prime Minister asked MND to consider additional housing support for larger families, who often need bigger, costlier homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Prime Minister recognised that larger families often need bigger homes, which cost more, and asked MND to consider additional housing support for them.

sections.label: Concern over larger flat competition
sections.summary: The speaker supports former private home owners buying HDB flats but worries these policies could increase competition for limited larger HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I support former private home owners being able to buy HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, I am concerned that the combined effect of these policies could increase competition for our limited stock of larger HDB flats – whether larger families may find it more difficult to afford the space they genuinely need.

sections.label: Tiered consent and VERS considerations
sections.summary: The speaker asks for consideration of tiered consent thresholds, 70 years for the VERS option, and upgrading costs against rejuvenation benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Consider similarly tiered consent thresholds, consider whether 70 years should be the point at which the VERS option arises, and consider the total cost of repeatedly upgrading an ageing estate against the benefits of rejuvenating the land and rebuilding for the needs of the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The policy choices we make for private and public housing affect each other.

sections.label: Relaxing collective sale threshold
sections.summary: The speaker believes relaxing the collective sale threshold is timely and necessary for owners to live comfortably and safely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It becomes a question of whether they can continue to live comfortably and safely in a home they have owned for decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This is why I believe the relaxation of the collective sale threshold is both timely and necessary.

sections.label: Shorter period to obtain signatures
sections.summary: The First Schedule, paragraph 2(1)(a), reduces the period for the CSC to obtain signatures to the CSA from 12 months to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, the First Schedule, paragraph 2(1)(a), reduces the period available to the CSC to obtain signatures to the CSA, from 12 months to six months.

sections.label: Extension for larger developments
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Minister consider a mechanism letting larger developments apply for an extension of up to nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Reaching every owner, explaining the proposal, answering questions and giving owners sufficient time to make an informed decision takes time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Therefore, I respectfully suggest that the Minister consider a mechanism allowing larger developments, for example, those with 250 or 500 units and above, to apply for an extension, perhaps up to nine months, where there are genuine practical difficulties.

sections.label: Collective sale for legacy developments
sections.summary: Section 84FC creates a collective sale mechanism for legacy residential developments where flat proprietors do not own the underlying land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Third, I welcome the introduction of section 84FC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This is an important provision because it creates a collective sale mechanism for certain legacy residential developments where flat proprietors do not own the underlying land, such as Neptune Court, Paterson Court and Townhouse Apartments, to name a few.

sections.label: Family's ageing apartment problems
sections.summary: The speaker's family bought an apartment in an already 30-year-old development and faced sewage, leakage, rubbish bin and lift problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: More than 25 years ago, my family bought an apartment in a development that was already around 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We encountered many of the problems associated with ageing developments: sewage problems, water leakage, rubbish bin choking and even a costly lift replacement programme.

sections.label: Why owners sold their flat
sections.summary: The flat was sold because the building was ageing, maintenance was costly, and the collective sale framework gave no realistic path.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We did not sell the apartment because we stopped loving the place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We sold the flat because the building was ageing, maintenance was becoming increasingly difficult and costly, and the existing collective sale framework did not give owners a realistic path forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For them, reducing the collective sale threshold to 70% is not merely a change in number.

sections.label: Mdm Phua's collective sale benefit
sections.summary: For 78-year-old Mdm Phua, a collective sale may mean avoiding 10 more years of stairs, leaks and expensive repairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For someone like 78-year-old Mdm Phua, it may mean that she no longer has to face another 10 years of climbing four flights of stairs, dealing with leaks and paying for increasingly expensive repairs simply because a collective sale could not previously obtain the required consensus.

sections.label: Lowered thresholds by development age
sections.summary: The Bill retains existing thresholds for younger developments but lowers them to 70% for ages 40 to 59 and 65% for 60 or more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill retains the existing thresholds for younger developments, but lowers them to 70% for developments aged 40 to 59 years and 65% for those aged 60 years or more.

sections.label: Question on threshold derivation
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry arrived at the 70% and 65% thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But it does mean the Ministry should explain how these thresholds were arrived at.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, my first question is: how did the Ministry arrive at these thresholds – 70% for a 40-year development and 65% at 60 years?

sections.label: CSC requisition threshold changes
sections.summary: The threshold to requisition a meeting to form a CSC rises to 35%, signature collection shortens to six months, and tighter restrictions follow an unsuccessful attempt.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The threshold required to requisition a meeting to form a CSC will rise to 35%; the period for collecting signatures will be shortened from 12 months to six months; and tighter restrictions will apply following an unsuccessful attempt.

sections.label: Aggregated reporting of collective sales
sections.summary: Aggregated reporting by age band, consent level and outcome would show where collective sale exercises get stuck and whether that changes under new thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Aggregated reporting by age band, consent level and outcome would allow us to see where collective sale exercises still get stuck and whether that changes under the new thresholds.

sections.label: Consent thresholds by development age
sections.summary: Thresholds stay unchanged below 40 years old, at 70% for 40 to 59 years, and 65% for 60 years or older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The present thresholds remain unchanged for developments below 40 years old – 90% for those who are 10 years and 80% for those between 10 and 39 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For developments that are 40 to 59 years old, the consent threshold will be 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For those that are 60 years or older, it will be 65%.

sections.label: Signature collection period shortened
sections.summary: The period to collect signatures will be six months instead of 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The period to collect signatures will be six months instead of 12.

sections.label: Guidance for older persons
sections.summary: Older persons, persons with mobility issues and caregiving families should receive clear guidance earlier from a neutral channel on decisions, moving, finances and help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They may worry about whether medical care will remain accessible, where their children live, whether shopping and getting around will be convenient, whether there are lifts and barrier-free facilities, and whether long-standing neighbourhood ties can be maintained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that older persons, persons with mobility issues and families with caregiving needs can receive clear guidance earlier from a neutral channel on when decisions must be made, when they may need to move, how finances should be arranged and where they can seek help if difficulties arise.

sections.label: Explaining planning parameters before investing
sections.summary: Before owners invest time and money, three matters should be explained: what planning parameters allow, what needs separate approval, and which figures are consultants' estimates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Others can continue to serve for many years after repairs, facility replacement, accessibility improvements and energy-efficiency upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, before owners invest substantial time and money, three matters should be explained separately and clearly: what existing planning parameters currently allow; which matters still require separate approval; and which figures are merely consultants' estimates based on market conditions.

sections.label: Good urban renewal principles
sections.summary: Good urban renewal should inform owners, help older residents, protect small businesses and make communities more liveable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Good urban renewal is not simply about replacing old buildings with new ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It should also give owners the information to make decisions, help older residents transition with peace of mind, ensure that small businesses are not overlooked and make redeveloped communities more liveable than before.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states that notwithstanding all the above, they support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: (In English): Notwithstanding all the above, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Lowering collective sale thresholds
sections.summary: The speaker supports lowering the threshold to 70% for developments aged 40 to below 60 years, and 65% for those 60 years or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deteriorating infrastructure may require redevelopments, and collective sale thresholds may need to fall as buildings age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is why I support the Bill's central reform, lowering the threshold to 70% for developments aged at least 40, but below 60 years, and to 65% for developments aged 60 years or more.

sections.label: Requisitioning meeting and retry limits
sections.summary: The threshold for requisitioning a meeting to constitute a CSC rises to 35%, with retries generally restricted for three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The threshold for requisitioning a meeting to constitute a CSC rises to 35%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: After a relevant unsuccessful event, another attempt will generally be restricted for three years unless stronger support is shown: 50% for the first early requisition and subsequently, the age-based threshold.

sections.label: Raising objectors' protection limit
sections.summary: The Bill raises from 0.25% to 0.5% of sale proceeds the aggregate limit the High Court must consider when adjusting distribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens protection for objectors by raising from 0.25% to 0.5% of sale proceeds, the aggregate limit the High Court must consider when adjusting distribution.

sections.label: Purchase price relevance exception
sections.summary: Under the Bill, purchase price remains relevant unless an owner bought after the CSC signed the sale and purchase agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, purchase price remains relevant unless an owner bought after the CSC signed the sale and purchase agreement.

sections.label: CSA execution period shortened
sections.summary: The Bill shortens the CSA execution period from 12 months to six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Bill shortens the CSA execution period from 12 months to six.

sections.label: 65% minority may sell
sections.summary: At 65%, a substantial minority may be required to sell without agreeing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: At 65%, a substantial minority may be required to sell without agreeing.

sections.label: Neutral guide and independent advice
sections.summary: The Government should provide a neutral guide and access to independent legal or financial advice, separate from CSC, marketing agent and purchaser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government should provide a neutral guide and access to independent legal or financial advice, separate from CSC, marketing agent and purchaser.

sections.label: Differentiated gradient older lower threshold
sections.summary: The idea is to have a differentiated gradient, so the older it is, the lower the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Members would remember that I said at the start, the idea is to have a differentiated gradient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the older it is, we lower the threshold.

sections.label: Signature collection period lowered
sections.summary: The signature collection period is lowered from 12 months to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, Members also asked about the signature collection period, lowered from 12 months to six months.

sections.label: Six-month period supported by data
sections.summary: The six-month period is supported by data collected from recent successful collective sale exercises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The six-month period is supported by data collected from recent successful collective sale exercises.

sections.label: Signature collection timing
sections.summary: Most signatures are gathered in the first four months or a concentrated one-to-two-month window.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: A significant majority of signatures are typically gathered within the first four months or within a concentrated window of one to two months during the signature collection period.

sections.label: Objecting owner financial loss
sections.summary: A collective sale cannot proceed if an objecting owner's proceeds, after deductions, are less than the original price paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Under the present rules in the Act today, a collective sale cannot proceed if it results in a financial loss to an objecting owner, and an objecting owner is considered to have incurred a financial loss if, amongst others, the proceeds of sale for their lot, after allowable deductions, are less than the price they originally paid for the unit.

sections.label: SSD for collective sale owners
sections.summary: Owners in a collective sale may incur SSD if the sale falls within the three-to-four-year holding period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Owners who participate in a collective sale may incur SSD if the sale occurs within the applicable SSD holding period, which ranges from three to four years depending on when the property was acquired.

sections.label: ABSD for replacement property
sections.summary: A Singapore Citizen who sold under a collective sale and owns no other residential property is not liable for ABSD on a replacement unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It may apply to some owners who are purchasing a replacement property following a collective sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But for a Singapore Citizen who has sold his/her existing property under a collective sale and does not own any other residential property at the time of purchasing a replacement residential unit, that person will not be liable for ABSD for the purchase of the replacement unit.

sections.label: Current milestone definition
sections.summary: The current milestone is tied to signing the sale and purchase agreement, when the purchase price is formally agreed with the purchaser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The current milestone, which is tied to the signing of the sale and purchase agreement, is the point at which the purchase price for the development has been formally agreed, crystalised, with the purchaser.

sections.label: Lawyer presence when signing
sections.summary: The requirement for a lawyer's physical presence when an owner signs the CSA was introduced in 2007 to address duress or misrepresentation concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, on the requirement, which is existing for the lawyers appointed for the collective sale to be present, when an owner signs the CSA in Singapore, a point Mr Ang Wei Neng raised, let me just say that this is not just a matter of witnessing or a formal evidential requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We introduced the requirement for the physical presence of a lawyer in 2007 to address concerns that some owners were pressed to sign the CSA under duress or misrepresentation.

sections.label: Signing arrangements for mobility issues
sections.summary: CSC can work with appointed lawyers to make special signing arrangements for individuals in Singapore with mobility issues or needing assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If needed or necessary, CSC can already work with the appointed lawyers, to make special arrangements to accommodate signing by individuals in Singapore, who may face mobility issues or might, for some reasons, require additional assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I would add that the requirement of a physical presence of a lawyer only applies where the CSA is signed in Singapore, not when it is signed overseas.

sections.label: No prescriptive law on provisions
sections.summary: The law need not be prescriptive on what is provided, by whom and when, as each development's owners have different considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Beyond this, we do not see a need for the law to be prescriptive on what exactly you provide, by who and at what juncture, because each set of owners within each development will have different considerations.

sections.label: Twelve months after sale threshold
sections.summary: After the collective sale threshold is reached, owners have up to 12 months to find a buyer and submit to the STB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For example, even after the collective sale threshold is reached, owners then have up to 12 months to find a prospective buyer and make submissions to the STB, and this is also time to review their applications.

sections.label: Clarifying development potential benefits
sections.summary: Clarifying the site's development potential reduces misalignment with buyers and improves prospects of a sale agreement; the framework will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ultimately, it is in the interest of the CSC and owners to clarify the development potential of the site, as it reduces misalignment with potential buyers, and also improves the prospects of a successful sale and purchase agreement being concluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will review the collective sale framework, taking into account feedback from all stakeholders and the suggestions given by various Members today.

sections.label: Reference date for consent thresholds
sections.summary: Reference is taken from the date of completion of the latest building, so the newest unit remains subject to consent thresholds for the minimum period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What we have done is: we take reference from the date of completion of the latest building and this ensures that the newest unit in the development will then still be subject to the respective consent thresholds for at least the prescribed minimum period of time.

sections.label: Deeming provision for flat lessees
sections.summary: The proposed 127(3A) inserts a deeming provision that agreement of 25% of flat lessees binds the rest and registers the strata title application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new proposed 127(3A) is a clarification amendment, which inserts a deeming provision that the agreement of this 25% of flat lessees will bind the remaining flat lessees and cause the strata title application to be registered, on par with the existing sections 125(6) and 126(5).

sections.label: Strata Management Act review update
sections.summary: MND oversees the review and BCA has completed public consultation on proposed areas of review of the Building (Strata Management) Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Yeo, I think, asked about the sinking funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This review is overseen by MND and I understand that BCA has completed a round of public consultation on the proposed areas of review of the Building (Strata Management) Act and will provide an update when ready.

sections.label: VERS and collective sale support
sections.summary: The Government will support VERS when brought to the House, and MND will share collective sale learning points with MinLaw.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Having said that, I accept what Ms Cassandra Lee says about there being learning points between both the public as well as the private market, and these are factors that will be taken into account, and at the appropriate time, the relevant Ministry will come back with VERS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I want to assure Members as well that when we put up a programme, whether it is a Bill like this to amend the collective sale framework, or eventually, when VERS is brought to this House, it will have the support of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MND will talk to MinLaw, we will share our experiences on the collective sale regime and the learning points will be shared across the different agencies.

sections.label: Two issues not conflated
sections.summary: The two issues should not be conflated, and improvements will continue to keep the regime fit for purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so, I hope the Members understand that the two issues are not to be conflated, and to try and do so, I think, represents a too simplistic and as I said, an unrealistic approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will continue to make the necessary improvements to the regime, to ensure that it continues to be fit for purpose, meets Singapore's objectives and allows us the ultimate objective of rejuvenation and renewal in land-scarce Singapore.

sections.label: Bill facilitates urban renewal
sections.summary: The speaker is in favour of urban renewal and says this Bill facilitates the urban renewal process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I think I was just drawing the analogy that Singaporeans are concerned about the use of our land and the competing demands for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: And I did say that I am in favour of urban renewal and therefore, this Bill is another feather in our cap that we can use to facilitate the process of urban renewal.

sections.label: Land sources for redevelopment
sections.summary: The speaker set out the broader picture of urban redevelopment and renewal, citing brownfield redevelopment and en bloc sales as land sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I was just trying to set out the broader picture of urban redevelopment and urban renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: And I think that there are many sources for land that we can find in Singapore – brownfield redevelopment or en bloc sales of private properties.

sections.label: Clarification on linking issues
sections.summary: The Member seeks clarification that the two issues ought not be linked, though he thinks they are linked indirectly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, I am just seeking clarification that, in fact, those two ought not be linked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I do think the issues are linked, albeit not directly, which the Minister seems to be insinuating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I think the insinuation that I understood from the Minister's closing speech was that if we had implemented this collective sale regime earlier, potentially, we could have saved Maju Forest.
